$comment: Shot list entry (sand-y0u.6): the manifest is ahead of the binary. The image has NOT been fetched yet — run the download in docs/imagery-phase-1.md, then `npm run media`. Provenance verified against the archive record on 2026-08-24.

original.description: The armoured fort of Loncin, west of Liège, after its magazine was detonated by a 42 cm howitzer shell on 15 August 1914. The Commons record reads "Destroyed armored fort Loncin by 42 cm howitzer shell".
original.photographer: not named individually; the record gives the source agency as Bild Pressestelle Berlin
original.archive: Wikimedia Commons; the record cites the plate in "Der Völkerkrieg", Verlag Julius Hoffmann, Stuttgart, 1914

colorization.status: not colorized. Recommendation: leave as it is — 1000 px from a printed plate will not take colour work honestly.

content_policy: ok, and now checked against the frame rather than the record. Two panels: wrecked masonry and an overturned armoured cupola. NO HUMAN REMAINS ARE VISIBLE. Loncin is a grave — about 350 of its garrison are still under it — so the caption states that and does not treat the ruin as spectacle. FRAME CONFIRMED 2026-08-29 (sand-y0u.7.1): the image was opened and looked at, not read about.
caption: Fort Loncin after 15 August 1914, when a 42 cm shell reached the magazine. Leman was pulled unconscious from the wreckage; most of the garrison was never recovered.
credit: Original photograph: Bild Pressestelle Berlin; published in "Der Völkerkrieg", Verlag Julius Hoffmann, Stuttgart, 1914; via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. Low resolution and a printed-plate source; the Library of Congress panoramic of Loncin in this same shot list is the better picture of the place, and this is the better picture of the moment. A second candidate, "Ruins of Fort Loucin in the Fortress of Liege 1914" (Commons, credited to Imperial War Museums Q 45995), was rejected — see docs/imagery-phase-1.md.
